newsitem.title: USA: Colonial Pipeline to hike shipping tariffs July 1.
newsitem.headline: Colonial Pipeline to hike shipping tariffs July 1.

text.p: Colonial Pipeline told shippers Tuesday that it will boost its rates by 1.6583 percent on July 1.
The increase will cover inflation seen in the past 12 months as reflected by the by the Producer Price Index for Finished Goods, the company said.

The rate under the new tariff for transporting a barrel of gasoline, kerosene or diesel fuel from Houston, Texas, to New York Harbor will increase to $1.0546 from $1.0374. That puts the resulting per-gallon cost at 2.51 cents for the 1,541-mile delivery.

The Houston-to-New York Colonial Pipeline is the largest refined products pipeline in America. A consortium jointly owned by 10 oil companies, Colonial pumps a total of 2.1 million barrels per day of gasoline and distillates, ar nearly 20 percent of total daily U.S. refined products demand.
